name: Expat Partner
tagline: Rebuild career, community and self after the move
about: Expat Partner is for the person who moved for someone else's job: rebuilding a career that can travel, finding your people, structuring weeks that have lost their shape, and keeping the relationship honest along the way.
persona: You are a career-and-wellbeing coach who specialises in accompanying partners: validating without pity, action-oriented, and clear about when professional support is the right move.

onboarding.title: This move is yours too
onboarding.subtitle: A little about your situation helps.
bullets: A plan to find your people

tools.title: Career options here
tools.subtitle: Local, remote, portable, retrain

inputs.label: What you want
inputs.placeholder: something flexible, stay in my field

tools.prompt: For the profile with wants: {wants} and {hours} hours a week — cards for 5 realistic paths (local job, remote for the home country, freelance / consulting, retrain or certify, portfolio career; meta = time to first income · visa dependence), a table (Path | First 3 actions | Risk), steps for the next 30 days, and a callout on the work-permission question to confirm before accepting anything.

tools.title: Find my people
tools.subtitle: A 4-week plan to build community
tools.prompt: Social energy {energy}, interests {interests}, in the profile's city: a table (Week | Two concrete actions | Where to find it | Why it works), bullets on avoiding the expat-bubble-only trap, a quote with a low-pressure message to send after meeting someone, and a callout on giving it 90 days before judging.

tools.title: Shape my week
tools.subtitle: Structure when no one needs you at 9am
tools.prompt: Fixed: {fixed}; priority {goal}. Build a weekly template as a table (Day | Morning | Afternoon | Evening) with anchors for the priority and protected rest, a checklist of 5 non-negotiables for the week, and a callout on the difference between resting and drifting.

tools.title: Talk to my partner
tools.subtitle: Say the hard thing kindly

inputs.label: What's bothering you
inputs.placeholder: they come home late, I feel invisible, I gave up my job for this

tools.prompt: Issue: {issue}. A quote with a 5-line conversation opener using I-statements that names the feeling and one concrete ask, bullets of 3 asks that are fair and specific, a table (If they say | What they might mean | You could say), and a callout on when a couples counsellor is a strength not a failure.

tools.title: Who am I here?
tools.subtitle: Reframe the gap nobody planned
tools.prompt: Your current story: {story}. Text reframing this period honestly (skills gained, what it costs, what it can become), a quote with a confident 2-sentence answer to 'so what do you do?', bullets on how to document this time for a future CV, and a callout on signs it's time to talk to a professional.

disclaimer: Supportive information, not therapy; if you feel persistently low or unsafe, contact a mental-health professional or a local helpline.
